extracted.intended_audience: attorneys authorized to practice before the USPTO; OED staff and disciplinary counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Final Order imposing reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24: describes suspension, required notices, operational effects (Customer Numbers/PKI), and procedural findings when a respondent fails to respond. Targets imposition and implementation of discipline for attorneys before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of OED may request imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a state authority pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Notice and Order must be sent notifying the respondent and providing an opportunity to respond; the respondent may oppose imposition of identical reciprocal discipline based on the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond (40-day period) and notice delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order provides Respondent an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the state court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice should be served (here, by certified mail with receipt). Failure to file a response within the allotted time may be treated as an absence of a genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Finding of no genuine issue of material fact upon failure to respond
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the OED/Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where no genuine issue of material fact exists due to non-response, reciprocal discipline identical to the state-imposed sanction is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from practice before the USPTO (trademark and non-patent law)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is suspended for sixty (60) days from the practice of trademark and other non-patent law before the United States Patent and Trademark Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The suspension is effective the date of the Final Order; notice may specify that the respondent is not authorized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters (if so). The suspension is predicated on violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) and the state suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Notice in the Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish a Notice in the Official Gazette describing the suspension and its reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice should identify the respondent, summarize the suspension (duration, grounds, and relevant rules violated), and may provide a link to disciplinary decisions (e.g., OED FOIA Reading Room).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to state disciplinary agencies and courts per 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where Respondent is admitted, to courts where Respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This disseminates the discipline details to the appropriate state authorities and courts as required by regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 contains duties imposed on practitioners subject to public discipline (e.g., notice to clients, file handling obligations); respondent must follow those duties as part of the disciplinary order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation from USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO shall dissociate Respondent's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure ("PKI") certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative steps will be taken to remove the respondent's operational access tied to Customer Numbers and PKI credentials during suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor shall his name be added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until he is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This restriction prevents any controlled or indirect practice before the USPTO during the period of suspension until formal reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal authority for disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disciplinary decisions are issued under statutory and regulatory authority; citations should be included in orders and notices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive grounds for state suspension (example: Rule 20:8.4(c) misconduct)
rubrics_metrics.description: State suspension here was predicated on respondent's admission that he violated Wisconsin Supreme Court Rule 20:8.4(c) by preparing and executing, without authorization, numerous forms, checks and other documents relating to a trust and arranging unauthorized disbursals in the aggregate amount of several hundred thousand dollars.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serious misconduct involving unauthorized preparation/execution of trust documents and unauthorized transfers/disbursements can form the basis for suspension that will be the subject of reciprocal discipline proceedings.
